title: Landforms, Rocks and Minerals
seo_title: Primary 3 Basic Science: Landforms, Rocks and Minerals Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 3 Basic Science: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: Rocks are made of minerals; rocks are igneous, sedimentary or metamorphic; minerals have properties such as hardness, luster and colour; rocks and minerals are used by people; landforms are shaped by rocks. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 3, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): rocks and minerals, properties of minerals, how rocks form, uses of rocks and minerals and rock layers and investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Igneous rocks cool from magma; sedimentary rocks form in layers; metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure.
body_html:
How to think about it

Rocks are made of one or more minerals. Minerals are natural, non-living solids.

  • Minerals are identified by hardness (Mohs scale, talc 1 to diamond 10), colour, streak and lustre.
  • Igneous rocks form when magma or lava cools (granite, basalt).
  • Sedimentary rocks form from layers of sediment pressed together (sandstone, limestone) and may hold fossils.
  • Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure change rocks (marble, slate).
Example

A mineral scratches quartz. What do you know?

harder minerals scratch softer ones

Answer: it is harder than quartz

Example

Which rock type might have fossils?

fossils form in sediment layers

Answer: sedimentary

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a mineral's outside colour always matches its streak.
  • Mixing up rocks and minerals.
  • Thinking fossils are found in igneous rocks.

faq.q: What is the difference between a rock and a mineral?
faq.a: A mineral is one natural solid substance. A rock is made of one or more minerals.

faq.q: How do we test the hardness of a mineral?
faq.a: Try to scratch it with objects of known hardness, such as a fingernail, a copper coin, a steel nail and glass.

faq.q: Why is mining important in Nigeria?
faq.a: Nigeria mines limestone for cement, coal, tin and gold, but mines must be managed and cleaned up to protect farms, rivers and people.
